I farm only 5 mu, so I will keep the whole field in my usual wheat-maize rotation. That is the safest and most familiar way for me to manage the land, and with some family members working off-farm I do not want to add a new crop that needs more attention. I have farmed for 20 years, I have well irrigation, and I know this system well, so I will stay with improved seed and steady fertilizer use instead of taking big risks. For wheat, I will aim for a stable stand through the winter, use moderate water, and control weeds and disease with a small number of sprays. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize quickly on the same 5 mu so I do not lose time or soil moisture. For maize, I will use a little more nitrogen because it needs strong growth in summer, keep irrigation flexible with the well, and do a few pesticide applications because summer insects and weeds are usually stronger. I will use rotary tillage because it saves labor and fits my small farm and household situation.
